record.original_question: Characterize the representing measures for the origin in the unit ball in C^n .

evidence.quote: Problem 5.5.1 Characterize the representing measures for the origin in the unit ball in Cn .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B_n = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^n : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$, with topological boundary the unit sphere $S_n = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^n : |z| = 1\}$. Let $A(B_n)$ denote the ball algebra, that is, the uniform algebra of continuous complex-valued functions on the closed unit ball $\overline{B_n}$ that are holomorphic on $B_n$, equipped with the supremum norm.

A finite positive regular Borel measure $\mu$ on $S_n$ is called a representing measure for the origin (with respect to $A(B_n)$) if
$$ f(0) = \int_{S_n} f \, d\mu \qquad \text{for every } f \in A(B_n). $$

Give an intrinsic characterization of the set of all such representing measures for the origin on $S_n$.
artifact.category_tag: Representing measures for the ball algebra
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing all representing measures for the origin with respect to the ball algebra on the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$ is a classical question; many specific families of such measures are known (e.g., from work of Rudin, "Some representing measures for the ball algebra", Michigan Math. J. 1980), but a complete intrinsic characterization does not appear to have been established in the literature found by the search. Status could not be definitively confirmed.

status_evidence.title: Some representing measures for the ball algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Rudin, Michigan Math. J. 27 (1980), constructs and studies specific representing measures for the ball algebra on the unit ball in C^n.
status_evidence.claim: Specific families of representing measures are known, but the search did not surface a complete characterization.
